text:
Jared Spurgeon returned to Minnesota's lineup in mid-November after an injury, and the Wild have been winning with him back in it. At 36, past 1,000 games, all of them with Minnesota, he has 1 goal and 7 assists in 15 games.

The points are running ahead of his game. He is scoring 1.6 points per 60 minutes; our range for him is about 0.8 to 1.3. Minnesota has scored 7.6 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and that kind of good fortune does not usually last.

But the on-ice play is also good. The Wild get 60% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him out there, the share of chance quality, 10 points better than when he sits. Last season Evolving-Hockey rated him around replacement level overall but in the 93rd percentile at taking chances away, and that defensive side is what we would watch.

His minutes have come down, about 18.9 a night over his last ten, 3.2 below his season average. That is probably the right role now: a smart, careful defenseman whose value shows up more in what doesn't happen than in what does.
headline: Back, and still useful
